```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.paymenttermdiscount(amount numeric, currency_id numeric, paymentterm_id numeric, docdate timestamp with time zone, paydate timestamp with time zone)
 RETURNS numeric
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $function$
/*************************************************************************
 * The contents of this file are subject to the Compiere License.  You may
 * obtain a copy of the License at    http://www.compiere.org/license.html
 * Software is on an  "AS IS" basis,  WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, either
 * express or implied. See the License for details. Code: Compiere ERP+CRM
 * Copyright (C) 1999-2001 Jorg Janke, ComPiere, Inc. All Rights Reserved.
 *
 * converted to postgreSQL by Karsten Thiemann (Schaeffer AG), 
 * kthiemann@adempiere.org
 *************************************************************************
 * Title:	Calculate Discount
 * Description:
 *	Calculate the allowable Discount Amount of the Payment Term
 *
 *	Test:	SELECT paymenttermDiscount(110, 103, 106, now(), now()) FROM TEST; => 2.20
 ************************************************************************/

DECLARE
	v_Precision		NUMERIC := 0;
	v_Currency		NUMERIC := 0;
    v_Min			NUMERIC := 0;
	Discount		NUMERIC := 0;
	Discount1Date		timestamp with time zone;
	Discount2Date		timestamp with time zone;
	Add1Date		NUMERIC := 0;
	Add2Date		NUMERIC := 0;
	p   			RECORD;
BEGIN
	v_Currency := Currency_ID;
	IF (v_Currency = 0) THEN 
		SELECT COALESCE(MAX(C_Currency_ID),0) 
		INTO v_Currency 
		FROM AD_ClientInfo ci, C_AcctSchema s, C_PaymentTerm pt 
		WHERE ci.AD_Client_ID = s.AD_Client_ID 
		AND ci.AD_Client_ID = pt.AD_Client_ID 
		AND pt.C_PaymentTerm_ID = PaymentTerm_ID; 
	END IF;
	
	SELECT StdPrecision
	    INTO v_Precision
	    FROM C_Currency
	    WHERE C_Currency_ID = v_Currency;

	SELECT 1/10^v_Precision INTO v_Min;
	
	--	No Data - No Discount
	IF (Amount IS NULL OR PaymentTerm_ID IS NULL OR DocDate IS NULL) THEN
		RETURN 0;
	END IF;

	FOR p IN 
		SELECT	*
		FROM	C_PaymentTerm
		WHERE	C_PaymentTerm_ID = PaymentTerm_ID
	LOOP	--	for convineance only
		Discount1Date := TRUNC(DocDate + p.DiscountDays + p.GraceDays);
		Discount2Date := TRUNC(DocDate + p.DiscountDays2 + p.GraceDays);

		--	Next Business Day
		IF (p.IsNextBusinessDay='Y') THEN
			Discount1Date := nextBusinessDay(Discount1Date, p.AD_Client_ID);
			Discount2Date := nextBusinessDay(Discount2Date, p.AD_Client_ID);
		END IF;

		--	Discount 1
		IF (Discount1Date >= TRUNC(PayDate)) THEN
			Discount := Amount * p.Discount / 100;
		--	Discount 2
		ELSIF (Discount2Date >= TRUNC(PayDate)) THEN
			Discount := Amount * p.Discount2 / 100;
		END IF;	
	END LOOP;
	
	--	Ignore Rounding
	IF (Discount > -v_Min AND Discount < v_Min) THEN
		Discount := 0;
	END IF;

	--	Round to currency precision
	Discount := ROUND(COALESCE(Discount,0), v_Precision);
	
	RETURN	Discount;
END;

$function$
```

```sql
*

* tspc@dodo.com.au 
*/
DECLARE
	v_nextDate	date := trunc(p_Date);
	v_offset	numeric	:= 0;
	v_Saturday	numeric	:= TO_CHAR(TO_DATE('2000-01-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD'), 'D');
	v_Sunday	numeric	:= (case when v_Saturday = 7 then 1 else v_Saturday + 1 end);
	v_isHoliday	boolean	:= true;
	v_country       c_country.c_country_id%type;
	nbd C_NonBusinessDay%ROWTYPE;
begin
	v_isHoliday := true;
	loop
		SELECT	CASE TO_CHAR(v_nextDate,'D')::numeric 
					WHEN v_Saturday THEN 2
					WHEN v_Sunday THEN 1
					ELSE 0
				END INTO v_offset;
		v_nextDate := v_nextDate + v_offset::integer;
		v_isHoliday := false;
		SELECT COALESCE(MAX(co.c_country_id), 100) 
		INTO   v_country
		FROM   ad_client cl 
		       JOIN ad_language l ON cl.ad_language = l.ad_language 
		       JOIN c_country co ON l.countrycode = co.countrycode 
		WHERE  cl.ad_client_id = p_ad_client_id;
		FOR nbd IN	SELECT * 
					FROM C_NonBusinessDay 
					WHERE AD_Client_ID=p_AD_Client_ID and IsActive ='Y' and Date1 >= v_nextDate
					    AND COALESCE(C_Country_ID,0) IN (0, v_country)
					ORDER BY Date1
		LOOP
			exit when v_nextDate <> trunc(nbd.Date1);
			v_nextDate := v_nextDate + 1;
			v_isHoliday := true;
		end loop;
		exit when v_isHoliday=false;
	end loop;
	--
	return v_nextDate::timestamp with time zone;
end;
```

## Task
Propose at most 20 edge cases that would expose a wrong port: boundaries, NULLs,
unusual dates (month ends, leap days, daylight-saving changes in the session time zone), rounding
ties, and configurations the seed data lacks. The seed data is already sampled separately, so focus
on what it does not cover.

Each case gives `args` positionally, as strings in PostgreSQL input syntax or null:
  - amount (numeric)
  - currency_id (numeric)
  - paymentterm_id (numeric)
  - docdate (timestamp with time zone)
  - paydate (timestamp with time zone)
Timestamps with time zone may include an offset (e.g. 2026-03-08T01:30:00-08:00); without one they are
read in the session time zone.

A case may add up to 3 `fixtures`: synthetic rows inserted for that case only
(in a transaction that is rolled back). A fixture copies the row whose primary key is `clone_from`,
takes the new primary key `id` (must be between 990000 and 999999),
and overrides the columns in `set` (values as strings in PostgreSQL input syntax, or null). Fixtures
are allowed in: ad_client, c_acctschema, c_country, c_currency, c_nonbusinessday, c_paymentterm. The harness assigns unique name/value/uuid columns itself. Reference a
fixture from `args` by its id.

cases.name: null_stdprecision_currency
cases.rationale: The currency exists but its StdPrecision is NULL. ROUND(x, NULL) returns NULL even though a real discount of 2.20 was computed. A port that falls back to precision 0 or 2 would be wrong.

cases.name: spring_dst_elapsed_hours
cases.rationale: Adding 240 elapsed hours to 2024-03-01 23:30 PST lands on 03-12 00:30 PDT, so the deadline is 03-12 and paying on 03-12 gets the discount (2.20). Calendar-day addition would give a 03-11 deadline and 0.00.

cases.name: autumn_dst_elapsed_hours
cases.rationale: Adding 240 elapsed hours to 2024-11-01 00:30 PDT lands on 11-10 23:30 PST, so the deadline is 11-10 and paying on 11-11 gets 0.00. Calendar-day addition would give 2.20.

cases.name: utc_inputs_local_date
cases.rationale: docdate 05-01 03:00Z is 04-30 in Los Angeles, so the deadline is 05-10. paydate is 05-11 local, so the result is 0.00. A port that takes dates in UTC gets a 05-11 deadline and 2.20.

cases.name: currency_null_returns_null
cases.rationale: currency_id NULL skips the 0-fallback and the precision lookup finds no row, so v_Precision becomes NULL and the result is NULL, not 0.00.

cases.name: currency_zero_max_acctschema
cases.rationale: The currency_id 0 fallback takes MAX(c_currency_id) over all of client 11's acctschemas. That picks fixture currency 990001 (precision 0), so 2.345 rounds to 2. A port that uses the primary schema would give 2.35.

cases.name: currency_zero_missing_term_null
cases.rationale: currency_id 0 with a non-existent term: the fallback gives currency 0, there is no C_Currency row 0, so the precision is NULL and the result is NULL.

cases.name: amount_null_guard_unscaled_zero
cases.rationale: amount NULL returns the unscaled integer 0 even though currency_id is also NULL (which would otherwise give NULL). The text must be '0', not '0.00' or NULL.

cases.name: paydate_null_scaled_zero
cases.rationale: paydate is not covered by the NULL guard. Both comparisons are NULL, so the result is ROUND(0,2) = 0.00, not the unscaled 0 and not NULL.

cases.name: dead_zone_half_cent
cases.rationale: 0.25 * 2% = 0.005. ROUND would give 0.01, but the strict dead zone |d| < 0.01 forces 0.00.

cases.name: negative_half_away_rounding
cases.rationale: -117.25 * 2% = -2.345. Rounding half away from zero gives -2.35; banker's rounding or float arithmetic would give -2.34.

cases.name: tier1_zero_blocks_tier2
cases.rationale: Tier 1 (Discount 0, 5 days) matches, so the ELSIF is never reached and the 3% tier 2 is ignored. The result is 0.00, not 3.30.

cases.name: tier2_applies_after_tier1_deadline
cases.rationale: Paying after the tier 1 deadline (08-06) but before the tier 2 deadline (08-21) gives 110 * 3% = 3.30.

cases.name: next_business_day_saturday
cases.rationale: IsNextBusinessDay='Y'. The deadline 2024-06-15 is a Saturday, so it moves to Monday 06-17 and paying on 06-17 gets 2.20. Wrong weekday numbering would break this.

cases.name: holiday_chain_friday_weekend_monday
cases.rationale: The deadline is Friday 06-14, a holiday, so it moves to Saturday, then Monday 06-17 (also a holiday), then Tuesday 06-18. Paying on 06-18 gets 2.20. This exercises the re-loop and the chaining of consecutive holidays.

cases.name: foreign_country_holiday_ignored
cases.rationale: The holiday on Thursday 07-04 has c_country_id 101, which is not the client's derived country (100 via en_US), so it is ignored. The deadline stays 07-04 and paying on 07-05 gets 0.00.

cases.name: fractional_discount_days_cross_midnight
cases.rationale: DiscountDays 0.5 adds 12 hours to 13:00, giving 01:00 the next day. Paying the next day gets 2.20. Treating the days as integers or truncating them would give 0.00.

cases.name: null_gracedays_no_discount
cases.rationale: A NULL GraceDays makes both deadlines NULL, so neither comparison matches and the result is 0.00, even when paying the same day.

cases.name: precision3_exact_vmin_kept
cases.rationale: With precision 3, 0.05 * 2% = 0.001, which is exactly v_Min. The strict dead zone keeps it, and the result has scale 3: 0.001.
